scale.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000000000: מיליארד", "1000000000000: ביליון": the milliard is 10^9 and ביליון is 10^12. he.wikipedia "ביליון" (redirects to מיליארד): "מיליארד (1,000,000,000) הוא מספר טבעי השווה לאלף מיליונים"; "ב שיטת הספירה האמריקאית משמשת המילה ביליון במקום ה מילה" (only the American system uses ביליון for the milliard).

group_mark.source: CLDR main/he.xml defines no symbol of its own ("<group>↑↑↑</group>"). he.wikipedia "ביליון" (redirects to מיליארד) groups digits with a comma: "מיליארד (1,000,000,000)".

decimal_mark.source: CLDR main/he.xml defines no symbol of its own ("<decimal>↑↑↑</decimal>"). he.wikipedia "ביליון" (redirects to מיליארד) writes decimals with a point: "כ-2.5 מיליארד פעימות".

space_groups.source: he.wikipedia "ביליון" (redirects to מיליארד) groups digits with a comma, not a space: "מיליארד (1,000,000,000)".

plural_scale_needs_count.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "3000: <%%thousands< אלפים", the plural takes a count; "אלפים" alone names no number.

scale_noun_agrees.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "2000000: שני מיליון", "3000000: <%%spellout-numbering-m< מיליון": מיליון keeps the singular after every count.

joiner_tens_units.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "20: עשרים[ >%%and-feminine>];" with "%%and-feminine: 1: ו=%spellout-numbering=;": ו joins the unit to the ten (עשרים ושלוש). No source opened writes a ten and a unit without ו.

joiner_after_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "100: מאה[ >%%and-feminine>];" with the %%and-feminine rules "1: ו=%spellout-numbering=;" and "20: עשרים;": ו comes before a unit (מאה ואחת) but not before a ten (מאה עשרים). en.wiktionary "מאה" lists "עַד מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים" (up to 120), with ו before the ten.

joiner_between_groups.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: אלף[ >%%and-feminine>];" with the %%and-feminine rules "1: ו=%spellout-numbering=;" and "100: מאה;": ו comes before a unit (אלף ואחת) but not before a hundred (אלף מאה).

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: אלף[ >%%and-feminine>]" with "%%and-feminine: 1: ו=%spellout-numbering=;" and "500: חמש מאות;": ו goes before a unit, not before a hundred.

comma_between_classes.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: אלף[ >%%and-feminine>];" writes a space and no comma between two classes. No source opened shows a comma between two classes of one number, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1000: אלף[ >%%and-feminine>];" with the %%and-feminine rules "1: ו=%spellout-numbering=;" and "100: מאה;": ו comes before a last unit (אלף ואחת) but not before a round hundred (אלף מאה). So ו before the last group is optional.

ordinal_style.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50), spellout-ordinal-masculine: "10: עשירי;" then "11: =%%spellout-numbering-m=;": ordinal words exist only for 1-10; above ten the cardinal serves, so no ordinal has more than one word.

half_of_scale.source: he.wiktionary "חצי": "חלק אחד מתוך שניים . במספרים: ½ או 0.5." and "אַמָּתַיִם וָחֵצִי אָרְכּוֹ" (two cubits and a half): the half after ו is half of the unit before it. he.wikipedia "סטוקהולם": "כשני מיליון וחצי תושבים", the same after a scale word.

fold_marks.source: en.wikipedia "Niqqud": "In modern Israeli orthography, niqqud is mainly used in specialised texts such as dictionaries, poetry, or texts for children or new immigrants to Israel." en.wiktionary "שישה" gives the same number with and without points: "שישה / שִׁשָּׁה".

bidi_controls.source: CLDR main/he.xml writes the minus sign as "‎-": directional marks stand next to numbers in right-to-left text.

clitic_min_rest.source: The shortest Hebrew number word has two letters: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "6: שש;".

joiner_prefix.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "1: ו=%spellout-numbering=;", "2: ושתיים;": ו is written joined to the next word. en.wiktionary "כ־": "Like all one-letter words in Hebrew, כ־ functions as a clitic, attaching to the word that follows it."

clitic_prefix.source: en.wiktionary "כ־": "Like all one-letter words in Hebrew, כ־ functions as a clitic, attaching to the word that follows it." en.wiktionary "ה־": "( definite article ) The ."; "ב־": "In (a place or time)."; "ל־": "To ; the first part of a to-infinitive."; "מ־": "From , of , from inside ."; "כ־": "Like , as ."; "ש־": "Introduces a subordinate clause." en.wikipedia "Modern Hebrew grammar": "Several of Hebrew's most common prepositions are prefixes rather than separate words."

range_cue.source: en.wiktionary "בין": "between , among , amid". Usage notes: "A variety of terms may separate the two elements introduced by בין"; the most common is ל־, and "ו־ ( v'- , “ and ” ) exist as well".

article_one.source: en.wiktionary "ה־": "Traditionally, Hebrew nouns are considered to have three “states”: indefinite (“a(n)/some __”), definite (“the __”), and construct": the indefinite is the bare noun, with no article word.

minus_idioms.source: CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "-x: מינוס >>;" is the only minus rule. No source opened gives an idiom with מינוס that is no negative number.

of.source: en.wiktionary "שלושה": "שְׁלוֹשָׁה סְפָרִים ― sh'loshá s'farím ― three books"; CLDR RBNF, common/rbnf/he.xml (unicode-org/cldr, cldrVersion 50): "3000000: <%%spellout-numbering-m< מיליון". A count stands right before its noun or scale word, with no word between.

fraction_of.source: he.wiktionary "חצי": "בחול המועד נהוג לעבוד רק חצי יום.": a fraction stands right before the noun it divides, with no word between.

denominator_particle.source: he.wiktionary "חצי", fractions: "שש עשרית": a denominator above ten is one word form, with no particle.

class_noun.source: he.wikipedia "ביליון" (redirects to מיליארד): "מאות מיליארדי פרטים": after a collective the scale noun is plural; no singular noun names a class.

half_unit.source: he.wiktionary "חצי": "חצי יום" puts a half before a unit noun. The list holds no unit noun, so such a phrase reads as the half alone.

abbreviation.source: CLDR main/he.xml abbreviates month names with a geresh, not a period: "דצמ׳". No Hebrew number word is listed as an abbreviation.

lone_decimal_mark.source: he.wikipedia "ביליון" (redirects to מיליארד) writes a digit before the decimal point: "כ-2.5 מיליארד". No source opened writes a bare decimal point before the digits.
